checks.name: the project is named 'The Chessboard' and its main scene is chessboard.tscn
the nine actions exist with their keys: A/D/W/S and the arrows, Space, Enter, F, M, V
line.tscn, trace.tscn and plane.tscn still run on their own: '1.50 m', '1 kept', 'open', and none of them has a Chessboard
cube.tscn still runs on its own: its Cube is an instance of the cube part at (1.05, 1.37, 0.6), 12 outward triangles, orange
the organism's lattice is the same idea: 88 cells from a loop inside a loop, sharing 1 mesh with its one material
organism.tscn still runs on its own: one whole turn of the limb still takes 33 cells: '55 of 88 cells'
body.tscn still runs on its own: four pivots under the root, 25 nodes below it, the cube part among them
the cube part is unchanged: it runs cube.gd, 12 outward triangles, 0.5 m on every edge, a Body with a shape of 12 triangles
two instances are two nodes with two meshes and two shapes, and ONE material: the part's own, saved in its scene file
chessboard.tscn inherits plane.tscn: the root runs plane.gd, with A, B, Segment, Strip, Record, Face, Marble and Under; no Cube, no Organism, no Body
Chessboard is a plain Node3D on the ground at (-1.75, 0, -2) and runs chessboard.gd; it holds no node of its own in the scene file; the marble waits at (2.6, 0.1, 1.2), clear of the floor
the floor is 64 instances of the cube part, kept in `cubes` in the order they were made; 192 nodes hang below the board
index to position: the cube made at (x, z) stands at (x * 0.5, 0.25, z * 0.5) from the board, for all 64; x runs first: cube 1 is at x = 0.5, cube 8 starts the next row at z = 0.5
the floor is 4 m by 4 m and 0.5 m high: from (-2, 0, -2.25) to (2, 0.5, 1.75) in the room; A stands over cell (2, 4) and B over cell (5, 4)
the finished floor is the chessboard: 64 materials made in code, 2 colours, 32 cells light and 32 dark; count_materials() says 64
what the floor adds: 192 nodes, 64 meshes of 12 triangles (768 in all), 64 shapes and 64 materials: nothing is shared but the scene file
one cell is a ghost: the collider of cube (5, 5) is disabled and no other; it keeps its mesh, its shape and its colour, so the eye cannot find it
a ray sent down over cell (5, 4) meets that cube's Body at 0.5 m; over the ghost it meets the ground under the floor, at 0.00 m
M with B over cell (5, 4): the marble falls from one metre above B and rests on the cell: 'marble at 0.60 m'
B walked 0.5 m towards us, over cell (5, 5): the marble falls through the ghost to the ground and lies inside the cube: 'marble at 0.10 m'
one cube: 1 child, 3 nodes; it stands at (-1.75, 0.25, -2) in the room, on the ground, in the far left corner
one loop, a row: 8 cubes, 24 nodes, the last at x = 3.5; still one material
the loop inside the loop, the floor: 64 cubes, 192 nodes, the last at (3.5, 0.25, 3.5); with no material code all 64 wear ONE material, the part's orange
the part's material is shared: one cube's colour changed, and all 64 read the new colour; so does a cube instanced afterwards
one material made in code and given to every cube: 1 material; its colour changed once through cube 0, and all 64 changed
one material made for each cube: 64 materials; the same line changes cube 0 and no other: 1 dark, 63 light
duplicate() gives each cube a copy of what it had: 64 materials again, one colour
the part's material is orange again for whoever instances it next
each value of `rhythm` builds the same 64 cubes with 64 materials and 64 colliders, and every cube wears what colour_of(x, z) returns; 1, 2, 2 and 15 colours
0 every cell alike: all 64 are the light colour
1 chessboard: light where (x + z) % 2 is 0, dark where it is 1; all 112 pairs of side-by-side cells differ
2 stripes: dark where x % 3 is 0: columns 0, 3 and 6, 24 cells dark and 40 light; z does not enter the rule
3 hue: Color.from_hsv(float(x + z) / (2 * n), 0.8, 0.6): 15 values of x + z, from 0 to 14, so 15 colours; a hue step is 1/16 of the circle
the planted mistake: (x + z) / (2 * n) in whole numbers is 0 for every cell, so every cell is Color.from_hsv(0, 0.8, 0.6), red (0.6, 0.12, 0.12); with float() there are 15 values, up to 0.875
swap x and z and 0, 0, 30 and 0 cells change colour; turn the floor half round and 0, 0, 48 and 56 do: the stripes and the hue ramp both have a direction, the other two have none
equal steps of hue are not equal steps of light: the 15 bands' luminance runs from 0.167 (band 11) to 0.553 (band 3); pure yellow has 0.565 and pure blue 0.155, 3.7 times less
the gap is g = s - w with w = 0.5 m, and the marble is d = 0.2 m across, so g = d at s = 0.70; at s = 0.55 the marble rests on the two cubes (0.59 m), at s = 0.75 it lies on the ground (0.10 m)

dropped from 2 m: widening, the first spacing that passes is 0.680; narrowing, the last that passes is 0.680; to the millimetre it is 0.679, a gap of 0.179 m, 0.021 m less than the marble; at s = 0.65 the marble is neither on top nor through: it ends at 0.34 m
let go at 0.75 m: widening and narrowing agree again, at 0.700; to the millimetre the first spacing that passes is 0.700: g = d, as predicted, within 1 mm
